questions.q: Why do missing tags go unnoticed for months in practice?
options: A resource works exactly the same with or without its tags, so nothing fails or alerts anyone
Azure automatically deletes untagged resources, so the problem disappears on its own
Missing tags always cause an immediate error when a resource is created
Tags are required by Azure and cannot actually be left blank
questions.explain: Nothing breaks when a tag is missing, which is exactly why it can sit unnoticed until something downstream, like cost reporting, quietly stops working correctly.

questions.q: In the compliance-check script, what does ContainsKey($key) check that simply checking whether $tags exists would not?
options: Whether that one specific required tag key is present, even if the resource has other tags
Whether the resource has more than ten tags total
Whether the tag's value is spelled correctly
Whether the resource was created more than a year ago
questions.explain: A resource can have some tags and still be missing a specific required key — ContainsKey checks for that exact key, not just whether any tags exist.

questions.q: Why does the script check '-not $tags' before calling ContainsKey?
options: So it doesn't error out by calling .ContainsKey() on a resource that has no tags at all
So it skips resources that are too expensive to check
So it only checks VMs and ignores other resource types
-not $tags has no effect on the script's behavior
questions.explain: Calling .ContainsKey() on a null tags object would error, so the script checks for that case first and reports the resource as non-compliant instead.

questions.q: Why should the tag compliance script run on a recurring schedule rather than just once?
options: New resources get created every week, and a one-time cleanup wouldn't catch tags missing on those
Running it more than once would delete the resources it finds
A scheduled run is required by Azure for all PowerShell scripts
It only works correctly the second time it's run
questions.explain: A one-time pass only fixes today's gaps; new resources created afterward need the same check, which is why it's published as a scheduled runbook.

questions.q: What two required tags does this lesson's example subscription check for?
options: CostCenter and Environment
Name and ResourceGroup
Owner and ExpirationDate
SubscriptionId and TenantId
questions.explain: The script's $requiredTags list is CostCenter and Environment — a small, specific set of keys the subscription has decided must exist on every resource.
